Add a unique_id to the aurora abb powerone sensors so that the sensor can be registered in the entity registry. Furthermore, the user is also able to override the name of an entity in the entity registry. When set, the name of the entity registry is used in favor of the name the device might give itself.

pr_comments: Hey there @davet2001, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with a integration (`aurora_abb_powerone`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L38) for? Thanks!

I can see that hard coding an appended word could be a problem for some.

But I’m not 100% certain of the proposal to remove it entirely.

The inverters have many parameters that can be read, including voltage, frequency, temperature, cumulative energy, average power etc.  So far we just read instantaneous power, but there may be more in future.

I would prefer that the patch allow additional sensors as part of the integration without requiring a 2nd breaking change to do so.
Can we access the serial number or a device ID of some sort to provide a unique id to solve this problem of using two breaking changes?

Thanks @davet2001 and @springstan for taking care of my issue.
Yes, it's actually possible to read the serial number with aurorapy: https://gitlab.com/energievalsabbia/aurorapy/-/blob/master/aurorapy/client.py#L244

I hope it helps.
Thanks!

Thanks @ebaschiera for investigating my question! 👍 With the help of the serial number in conjunction with the sensor type I have added a unique id so that any user can override the name of the entity.

@davet2001 what do you think of this solution?

Solution looks good to me - if you have tested it on a real system, even better.  

If you need me to test it, I can, but not until 15/feb since it needs daylight to test any comms.

Dave

Thanks @davet2001!
Have not tested it yet unfortunately, @ebaschiera could you test my PR?

Thanks again @davet2001 for the offer, I would not mind waiting a couple more days if @ebaschiera cannot test it himself.

Sorry, I cannot test the PR. Let's wait for @davet2001 's help.
Thanks!
Absolutely fine @ebaschiera! No worries at all.

I have just tried this patch on my HA Core install.

The new code requires the inverter to respond to client.serial_number() during HA startup.  But this doesn't happen during darkness.  When I started HA I got a long delay followed by this:
````
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]: 2020-02-14 21:25:13 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.sensor] Error while setting up aurora_abb_powerone platform for sensor
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]: Traceback (most recent call last):
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:   File "/home/homeassistant/dev/home-assistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 179, in _async_setup_platform
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:     await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(task), SLOW_SETUP_MAX_WAIT)
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:   File "/usr/lib/python3.7/asyncio/tasks.py", line 416, in wait_for
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:     return fut.result()
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:   File "/usr/lib/python3.7/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 57, in run
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:     result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:   File "/home/homeassistant/dev/home-assistant/homeassistant/components/aurora_abb_powerone/sensor.py", line 43, in setup_platform
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:     devices.append(AuroraABBSolarPVMonitorSensor(client, name, "Power"))
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:   File "/home/homeassistant/dev/home-assistant/homeassistant/components/aurora_abb_powerone/sensor.py", line 53, in __init__
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:     self._unique_id = f"{client.serial_number()}-{typename}"
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:   File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/aurorapy/client.py", line 251, in serial_number
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:     response = self.send_and_recv(request)
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:   File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/aurorapy/client.py", line 577, in send_and_recv
Feb 14 21:25:13 grey.lan hass[9130]:     raise AuroraError("Serial line closed")

````
It looks like the Aurora ABB component will fail to initialise if HA restarts during the dark.

It is an odd constraint, but I think this specific component needs to be able to initialise successfully even if there are no communications, ready for when the sun rises.

A possible option would be to use a dummy ID until comms came back online. I don't know the rules of the HA backend, but I suspect we are not allowed to change the value that unique_id() returns.

Perhaps we could use the com port and address as the unique ID?, ie.

````
        self._unique_id = f"{client.serline.port.replace('/','')}"\
            f"-{client.address}-{typename}"
````
This information is unique and available even when the inverter is off.

Thanks for testing this patch @davet2001!

Had no idea that this component would fail while stating during the dark.

> A possible option would be to use a dummy ID until comms came back online. I don't know the rules of the HA backend, but I suspect we are not allowed to change the value that unique_id() returns.

Yeah I would agree using a dummy value is not very clean and not the best option either.

However, I like your idea of using the address and the com port for the unique_id, because it solves the problem of initalising this component during the dark.
      

>  ```python
> self._unique_id = f"{client.serline.port.replace('/','')}"\
> f"-{client.address}-{typename}"
> ```

Have you tested this proposal already and what value or format do com port and address return?
I would suggest to use the slugify method to sanitize the data:
https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/f3a8196fb5815fc2abbcc6f4f2f4ab0e0758f067/homeassistant/util/__init__.py#L47-L49

Consequently, something along the lines of:
```python
self._unique_id = f"{slugify(client.serline.port)}-{client.address}-{typename}"
```

Yes, I’ve tested with the mod I proposed and it initialises ok.  The string is as would be expected based on the contents of configuration.yaml.

I think your slugify option looks good. If you can update the PR I will test today in the light and tonight in the dark.

Dave

Okay that is great to hear, hopefully this will work just as flawlessly.

I have updated the PR with https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/31649/commits/7fd5d2a22d9eee1aec5dd22f7b8225cc02671886 to include my suggestion of using slugify. Thanks again for testing this! 👍

PR tested, works in the dark (i.e. it initialises without raising exceptions).

When it runs it creates a new entity sensor.solar_pv_power_2

I assume this is unavoidable and due to the fact that there is a new underlying unique_id that HA has never seen before.

It means that users will need to do some renaming.

Will test in the daylight tomorrow.

It works in daylight too.

I had to reconfigure Lovelace by reconfiguring all cards with a reference to the old id.

I don’t know if there is a way to avoid this breaking change but that would be the only improvement I could think of.
But overall: ok to merge from my point of view.

That is great to hear, thanks @davet2001!

Yeah, absolutely agree with your point, @frenck is it normal that the entity id of a preexisting sensor changes when a unique id is added?
Closing this PR as it is currently impossible to provide a unique_id for this sensor.

review_comments: This is a com port and cannot be used as a unique ID .
So just use the client address and the typename? Since the typename is different for every sensor, see https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/31649#issuecomment-583790323

Or am I misunderstanding the following part of the documentation?

> If a device has a single serial but provides multiple entities, combine the serial with unique identifiers for the entities. For example, if a device measures both temperature and humidity, you can uniquely identify the entities using {serial}-{sensor_type}.

Thought I did the same with the use of the typename which represents the sensor type.

If the issue with using the slugified com port is that it might overlap with something else, then I’m not sure how to guarantee a unique ID other than adding the component name as part of the unique ID (eg a prefix). 

There is no MAC address and we can’t guarantee that the device responds at HA startup (so we can’t read its serial number).

> If the issue with using the slugified com port is that it might overlap with something else, then I’m not sure how to guarantee a unique ID other than adding the component name as part of the unique ID (eg a prefix).

I do not think that it can overlap with anything else since it is limited to this integration and this platform according to the [documentation](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/entity_registry_index/#unique-id-requirements). Pretty sure a combination of client.address and typename would be enough to fulfill all requirements of a unique_id since every other registered sensor would have a different typename so all of them would have their own indepent unique id.

Ok, then that seems fine to me.

@balloob can confirm hopefully.

If the device is disconnected and a different device is connected using the same port as the disconnected device, there's no way of telling them apart, right? I think that's the problem Paulus is aiming at.

This is why we eg don't allow using ip addresses as unique_id.

That makes a lot more sense, thanks for the explanation!
```python
self._unique_id = f"{client.address}-{typename}"
```
Without using the port it should be fine right?

https://gitlab.com/energievalsabbia/aurorapy/-/blob/master/aurorapy/client.py#L534

`client.serial_number()` would be perfect but it is not available during the night, see https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/31649#issuecomment-586495192
We can't guarantee that the serial line address is unique if there is more than one device, right?
Yeah, you are right. So should I close this PR or is there any other option?
Yeah, unfortunately, it looks like that's best for now. :+1:
